hbp_bp_support.name: Cardio Essentials BP Support
hbp_bp_support.key: Per 3 capsules: 750 mg olive leaf, 750 mg black garlic, 300 mg celery seed, 200 mg grape seed (all extracts)
hbp_bp_support.src: Label: Cardio Essentials BP Support sell sheet ND681 Rev. 10/24 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Cardio Essentials BP Support SS ND681.pdf), opened with the Dropbox reader on 2026-11-03 and again for the review fixes the same day. Supplement Facts: serving size 3 capsules, 30 servings per container; olive leaf extract (Olea europaea, 16% oleuropein, Benolea EFLA 943) 750 mg; fermented black garlic bulb extract (Allium sativum, >1% S-allyl cysteine) 750 mg; concentrated celery seed fraction (Apium graveolens, 42.5% phthalides, 3nB) 300 mg; grape seed extract (Vitis vinifera, 90% polyphenols, MegaNatural-BP) 200 mg. Directions 'Take three capsules daily or as directed by your healthcare practitioner.' Caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' The sheet's compliance line is 'Support for healthy blood pressure already in the normal range', and it says Benolea and MegaNatural-BP work by promoting nitric oxide production. Size R182 90C: products DB (ND144 price list 10/1/26). Protocol: Asher's Hypertension protocol email (2021-03-11) names it as the formula; his Drive protocol sheet (2023-02-13): 'BP Support if looking purely for blood pressure support'. The label sets no time of day; the evening meal is this sheet's plan, to spread the pills. Name: a no-break space holds 'BP Support' together, so the name wraps after 'Essentials' as the bottle reads. URL: the product key cardio-essentials-bp-support-r182 was seen through web search on NutriDyn storefronts that share the catalog; nutridyn.com itself is blocked from this session, so the main-site page was not opened. Photo: build/img-src/R182.png is a 348x640 smooth 4x stopgap (Lanczos with light sharpening, no AI) of the 87x160 chart thumbnail (scratchpad products/img/R182.png), listed in img-src/soft.json, so the build prints it under SOFT PRODUCT PHOTOS. Checked by eye: it is the Cardio Essentials BP Support bottle. Its real detail is still 160 px, about 163 ppi at the 0.98 in print height. The print master has to come from Asher, or from Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R182_Web (a 65 KB web render) or the ND143 catalog artwork; the Dropbox download host is refused from these sessions. Stage it as build/img-src/R182.png and take R182 out of soft.json.

hbp_nitric_boost.name: Nitric Boost
hbp_nitric_boost.key: Per 3 capsules: 375 mg beet root extract, potassium nitrate (150 mg potassium), 120 mg magnesium, 300 mg vitamin C, 100 mg B1, plus D3, B12, zinc, pomegranate, tart cherry, pine bark and grape seed
hbp_nitric_boost.src: Label: Nitric Boost sell sheet ND1255 Rev. 6/25 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/Nitric Boost SS ND1255.pdf), opened with the Dropbox reader on 2026-11-03 and identical to scratchpad labels/labels.json R257. Supplement Facts: serving size 3 capsules, 30 servings; vitamin C (as magnesium and zinc ascorbate) 300 mg; vitamin D3 15 mcg; thiamin 100 mg; vitamin B12 50 mcg; magnesium (as magnesium ascorbate) 120 mg; zinc 7 mg; potassium (as potassium nitrate) 150 mg; beet root extract 375 mg; pomegranate extract (Pomanox, 30% punicalagins) 200 mg; Montmorency tart cherry extract 200 mg; French maritime pine bark extract (Pycnogenol) 50 mg; grape seed extract (95% proanthocyanidins) 50 mg. The serving line names every label ingredient (amounts for the five that matter most for a medicine check, names for the rest) so a pharmacist can spot a doubled vitamin D or zinc; its pine bark and grape seed are named in the check panel's blood-thinner note, and its magnesium (120 mg) and zinc (7 mg) in the 4-hour spacing note. Directions 'Take three capsules daily or as directed by your healthcare practitioner.' Caution: pregnant, nursing or taking medication, consult. The sheet: 'By increasing nitric oxide production, the formula promotes vasodilation, supports healthy blood flow'; 'supports healthy nitric oxide production and optimal blood flow'; 'Beet Root Extract is rich in nitrates that convert to nitric oxide'. Size R257 90C: ND144 price list 10/1/26 (labels.json corroboration). Protocol: NutriDyn GLC 2025 endothelial-dysfunction protocol, slide 12 (HBP Supplement Recommendations: 'Nitric Oxide Strips suboptimal and/or hypertension, add Cardio Flow 1 scoop QD, Nitric Boost 3 caps/day'); a practitioner protocol Asher relayed by email, 2026-09-23: Nitric Boost for patients who will not take a powder. Why not Cardio Flow Powder (R157), the closer match to the competitor's L-citrulline category: only its photo. Dropbox /NutriDyn/Product Images/Product Images (1)/R157_Web1 exists, but this session's egress policy refuses the Dropbox download host (403 on CONNECT, rechecked 2026-11-03), so even the web render could not be fetched, and without a photo the column would print the grey placeholder. Swap column 2 once an R157 print photo is staged: Cardio Flow sell sheet ND535 Rev. 09/25 (opened 2026-11-03): about 1 scoop (15.5 g), about 30 servings; L-arginine 3 g, L-citrulline 3 g, beet root powder 2 g, hibiscus flower powder 1.5 g, taurine 1 g, grape seed extract 200 mg, magnesium (Albion bisglycinate) 100 mg, folate 200 mcg DFE; directions 'Mix 1 scoop in 12 ounces of water'; caution 'If you have had a heart attack, consult your physician before use' (that line goes into rx), and its 100 mg magnesium replaces Nitric Boost's 120 mg in the magnesium total. Morning with food per the GLC 2025 protocol ('with food') and the daytime rhythm. Its 120 mg magnesium is why the Magnesium Glycinate column drops to 1 capsule (total 250 mg a day, under the NIH 350 mg supplement upper limit). URL: product key nitric-boost-r257 seen through web search on a NutriDyn storefront (same catalog); nutridyn.com is blocked here, so not opened. Photo R257.png is a 328x640 Lanczos stopgap of the 82x160 chart thumbnail (img-src/soft.json): SOFT. Dropbox R257_Web (53 KB web render) is unreachable for the same reason; the print master has to come from Asher; stage it as build/img-src/R257.png.

hbp_mag_glycinate.name: Magnesium Glycinate
hbp_mag_glycinate.key: Per 2 capsules: 260 mg magnesium. Nitric Boost adds 120 mg, so 1 is enough.
hbp_mag_glycinate.src: Sheet-local copy of the shared mag_glycinate entry so this sheet can set its own dose without changing other sheets. Products DB R871 (13 switch-chart label reads of catalog ND143 10/1/26): 260 mg magnesium per 2 capsules as di-magnesium malate and magnesium lysinate glycinate chelate, plus 660 mg malic acid; directions 'Take two capsules twice daily'; sizes R871 60C, R871L 120C, R872 160C, R872L 320C (ND144 price list 10/1/26). The chelate maker, Albion, is recorded in the live panel read in Asher's magnesium blast (repo blasts/2026-10-12-magnesium-bp.html, which also records nutridyn.com/magnesium-glycinate as 'curl-200 8/11'); it left the serving line in polish round 1 to make room for the dose reason. The serving line starts with the label serving (2 capsules, 260 mg magnesium as di-magnesium malate and magnesium lysinate glycinate chelate; the form is left to the product name, since 'chelated' wrapped the line to five lines and grew the row), then says on the sheet why this plan uses less than the label: Nitric Boost already adds 120 mg, so 1 capsule (130 mg) is enough; the dose bar adds '2 if you skip Nitric Boost'. A patient holding the bottle ('Take two capsules twice daily') sees the reason beside the dose. Dose: a deliberate practitioner-directed dose below the label's 'two capsules twice daily' (520 mg): 1 capsule (130 mg) at bedtime because Nitric Boost already gives 120 mg, so the full plan supplies 250 mg of supplemental magnesium a day; 2 capsules (260 mg) without Nitric Boost. Both stay under the NIH ODS Tolerable Upper Intake Level of 350 mg a day from supplements for adults (Magnesium fact sheet for health professionals); the label amount would exceed it. The blast's 2025 Hypertension meta-analysis (38 RCTs) found no dose-response and the benefit in treated hypertensives (-7.7 mm Hg systolic) and magnesium-deficient patients, hence the test-first bullet. Protocol: NutriDyn GLC 2019 HBP protocol (Taming the Silent Killer): 1 capsule two to three times daily with food. Photo R872.png: the 244x420 original web render (the AI upscale was withdrawn 2026-11-03 because AI upscales rewrote label text), about 428 ppi at the 0.98 in print height.

hbp_omega_1000.name: Omega Pure EPA‑DHA 1000
hbp_omega_1000.key: Per softgel: 1,000 mg EPA + DHA (730 mg EPA, 270 mg DHA)
hbp_omega_1000.src: Products DB R243 (Pure, Designs for Health, Ortho Molecular and other switch-chart label reads of catalog ND143 10/1/26): EPA 730 mg + DHA 270 mg = 1,000 mg EPA + DHA per softgel; directions 'Take one softgel up to three times daily with food'; size R243 120S (ND144 10/1/26). Dose: 1 softgel at breakfast and 1 at dinner, one softgel per dose as the label reads, 2 a day in all. Protocol: the NutriDyn GLC 2025 endothelial-dysfunction protocol (slide 12) and the NutriDyn GLC 2019 HBP protocol (Taming the Silent Killer) use Omega Pure EPA-DHA 720 (R841), 2 softgels three times daily; this sheet uses the same Omega Pure line at 1,000 mg per softgel because it gives the omega-3s in fewer softgels and is the only Omega Pure bottle with a print-ready photo (R841 has only the 86x160 chart thumbnail here). 2 softgels a day (2,000 mg EPA + DHA) sits inside the label's up-to-3 and in the 2 to 3 g/day range a 2022 dose-response meta-analysis linked to the largest blood pressure effect (Zhang X et al., J Am Heart Assoc 2022;11:e025071, PMID 35647665: optimal 2 to 3 g/day). URL slug from products.py SLUGS (NutriDyn 60-day protocol doc). Name uses a non-breaking hyphen and space so 'EPA-DHA 1000' never splits. Photo R243.png: the 244x420 original web render (the AI upscale was withdrawn 2026-11-03 because AI upscales rewrote label text), about 428 ppi at the 0.98 in print height.

hbp_coq10.name: CoQ10 100 mg
hbp_coq10.key: Per softgel: 100 mg CoQ10, 67 mg vitamin E, 698 mcg RAE vitamin A (as beta-carotene)
hbp_coq10.src: Label: CoQ10 100 mg sell sheet ND270 Rev. 7/24 (Dropbox /NutriDyn/Sales/Practitioner Resource/NutriDyn Marketing Materials/CoQ10 100mg SS ND270.pdf), opened with the Dropbox reader on 2026-11-03 and again for the review fixes the same day. Supplement Facts: serving size 1 softgel, 60 servings; vitamin A (as beta-carotene, Betatene) 698 mcg RAE; vitamin E (as mixed tocopherols and d-alpha-tocopherol) 67 mg; coenzyme Q10 (CoQsol) 100 mg. Caution 'If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking medication, consult your healthcare practitioner before use.' The sheet lists 'Supports blood flow and nitric oxide production' and 'Supports energy production'. Directions, which source won: the label dose, 1 softgel daily. ND270 Rev. 7/24 prints 'Take one softgel daily', and two retail listings of the R350 label (web search, 2026-11-03) print 'Take one softgel daily or as directed by your healthcare practitioner'. Only the products DB's two switch-chart label reads (catalog ND143, 10/1/26, per the charts) print 'Take one softgel twice daily'. The sheet prints the dose a patient will find on the bottle; the NutriDyn GLC 2025 endothelial-dysfunction protocol (slide 12) and GLC 2019 HBP protocol use 1 softgel twice daily, which stays the practitioner's call (the sheet's Special considerations lines). The label sets no time of day; the evening meal is this sheet's plan, beside the other evening doses. Not checked against a physical R350 bottle: the ND143 catalog PDF (57 MB) is over the Dropbox reader's 5 MiB limit and nutridyn.com is outside these sessions' network allowlist. Vitamin A is printed in the label's unit, mcg RAE. Protocol: the HBP stack names 'CoQ10 (100 mg)', which is this product (CoQ10 Ubiquinol R350U is a different item). Size R350 60S (ND144 10/1/26 via the DB); at 1 a day a bottle lasts 60 days. URL: product key coq10-100-mg seen through web search on a NutriDyn storefront (SKU R350, same catalog); nutridyn.com is blocked here, so not opened. Photo: build/img-src/R350.png is a 368x640 smooth 4x stopgap (Lanczos with light sharpening, no AI) of the 92x160 chart thumbnail, listed in img-src/soft.json, so the build prints it under SOFT PRODUCT PHOTOS. Checked by eye: it is the CoQ10 100 mg bottle, not CoQ10 Ubiquinol. Real detail is still 160 px, about 163 ppi at print size. The print master has to come from Asher (Dropbox Product Images (1)/R350_Web and R350.png are 56 to 63 KB web renders, and the Dropbox download host is refused from these sessions); stage it as build/img-src/R350.png and take R350 out of soft.json. Never borrow img-src/coq10.png or R350U.png: that is CoQ10 Ubiquinol (R350U), a different bottle.
